messages:
sasha: Heads-up — just finished onboarding magnet-16k int4 to staging. Running longprefill stress (>20k tokens) and seeing output drift: model replays stale tokens from earlier prefix after a wrap event. Minimal repro and logs below. Anyone seen something like this recently?

liam: Can you paste the minimal repro + what exact flags you used for quant + kv-cache?

sasha: repro command:
```bash
python tools/repro_runner.py \
  --model magnet-16k-int4 \
  --mode prefill_and_stream \
  --context 32768 \
  --quant int4v2 \
  --kv-cache on \
  --prompt-file tests/longprefill/sample_22k.txt
```
observed logs (snippet):
```
[2026-03-23T15:12:10Z] prefill: writing kv shard 3 seq_base=21234 len=1024 fingerprint=0x1a2b3c4d
[2026-03-23T15:12:11Z] prefill: write complete shard=3 next_seq=22258
[2026-03-23T15:12:11Z] replay: reading kv shard 3 seq=21234 -> token_at_seq=...
[2026-03-23T15:12:11Z] kv: fingerprint mismatch shard=3 expected=0x1a2b3c4d got=0x1a2b3c4c
[2026-03-23T15:12:11Z] token_mismatch: prefix_token[21000] != replay_token[21000]
```

maya: hmm. fingerprint off-by-one on the tail looks like either a partial write or a wrap-around after kv-window shrink. Did you try the same run with q4_0 and int8?

sasha: quick checks: q4_0 gives the same logical drift but less frequent. int8 doesn't show repro on same inputs. So it's quant+window sensitive.

andre: likely suspects: (1) RoPE position scaling difference between prefill and replay code paths, (2) kv write/read fence not honoring seq_wrap when window resized, (3) a memcpy corner with int4 packing.

liam: agree. First quick thing — can you grep for any "wrap" or "shrink" messages near those timestamps? Also paste the exact model compilation flags (roperescale on/off).

sasha: compiled with: roperescale=enabled, roperescale_policy=auto, kv_window=32k->24k autoshrink on OOM. Grep shows:
```
[2026-03-23T15:11:58Z] kv: autoshrink triggered new_window=24576 cause=OOM
[2026-03-23T15:12:10Z] kv: prefill shard=3 write seq_base=21234 len=1024
[2026-03-23T15:12:11Z] kv: replay shard=3 read seq=21234 (wrap_adjusted=?)
```

maya: autoshrink during prefill is a red flag. If prefill wrote before shrink but replay reads after window adjusted, we need to ensure seq_base normalization is consistent. Also RoPE scale needs to be identical between prefill and replay — if roperescale_policy toggles with length, you'll get different embeddings.

liam: Can you run a tiny instrumented run that dumps the rotary phase scale and per-shard fingerprints before/after autoshrink? e.g. add env DEBUG_KV_DUMP=1 and attach the small JSON per-shard.

sasha: did that. dump attached (excerpt):
```
shard:3 {"seq_base":21234, "len":1024, "fingerprint":"1a2b3c4d", "rope_scale":1.0003}
shard:3 after_autoshrink {"seq_base":-120, "len":1024, "fingerprint":"1a2b3c4c", "rope_scale":0.9997}
```

andre: aha. seq_base negative after autoshrink? That indicates we normalize differently (we should never store negative seq_base). That explains fingerprint mismatch. Looks like the autoshrink path subtracts window_offset incorrectly.

liam: For a short-term mitigation, we can: (A) disable autoshrink on staging canary for new int4 onboards, (B) add an assertion in kv write path to reject negative seq_base, and (C) ensure rope_scale is snapshot-copied into the shard metadata at prefill time.

sasha: I've opened a ticket: INT4-KV-AUTOSHRINK-17688 (internal) with repro and dumps. Linking: https://redwood.internal/issue/INT4-KV-AUTOSHRINK-17688

ci-bot: Test run queued: CI/kv-regressions#17688 (staging) — will post results when finished. :gear:

liam: I'll own the quick assertion PR and add a unit test for negative seq_base (should error). Will also add a small test that runs prefill -> autoshrink -> replay to catch regressions.

andre: I'll prototype snapshotting rope_scale into shard metadata and a small canary that forces same scale on replay. If that fixes the delta, we can roll it into dedicated hotfix.

maya: Also recommend adding a longprefill smoke harness that runs |prompt| lengths 1k/10k/20k with quantization matrix (int4/q4_0/int8) so we catch these configuration-specific failures earlier.

sasha: agreed. For now I disabled autoshrink on the staging int4 canary and re-ran the failing sample — drift disappeared. Will keep the run up for 12h and report. Thanks all. :pray:

liam: great. pls ping when CI completes and when your 12h soak is done. I'll open the PR in 30m.

andre: PR/branch suggestion: fix/kv-normalize-autoshrink-17688. I'll add the rope snapshot commit on top as separate change.

sasha: noted. I'll add the testcases to the ticket and mark "blocking" for int4 onboard.

liam: :thumbsup:
